scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: OSPF routing on distribution switch switch_dist_1_1. The L3 gateway for Pod 1 (10.1.1.1 on br0) is not being advertised into the routing domain.

Mechanism: Host 10.1.1.2 can reach its default gateway 10.1.1.1 locally, and switch_dist_1_1 can ping the server farm via OSPF upstream routes. However, the rest of the network has no route back to 10.1.1.0/24, so return traffic (including ICMP time-exceeded and echo replies) cannot reach the host, producing timeouts beyond hop 1. This is confirmed by web_server_0 receiving “Destination Net Unreachable” from 10.200.0.1 when pinging 10.1.1.2, indicating the server access router lacks a route to 10.1.1.0/24.

Localization: switch_dist_1_1 FRR OSPF process. Evidence:
- switch_dist_1_1 OSPF config lacks the LAN: “router ospf … network 172.16.0.6/31 area 1” only; no “network 10.1.1.0/24” (frr_show_running_config).
- switch_server_access routing table has no entry for 10.1.1.0/24 (frr_show_ip_route).
- Traceroute from host_1_1_1_1: first hop 10.1.1.1 then all stars (no return path).
- Ping from web_server_0 to 10.1.1.2 returns “From 10.200.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable.”

Root cause: The OSPF advertisement for Pod 1’s user subnet (10.1.1.0/24) was removed or never configured on switch_dist_1_1.

Corrective fix: On switch_dist_1_1, add the missing OSPF network statement (or redistribute connected):
- vtysh: configure terminal; router ospf; network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1; end; write memory.
Verify 10.1.1.0/24 appears in OSPF on core and switch_server_access, then confirm bidirectional pings between 10.1.1.2 and server farm/Pod 2.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1 as the affected device in both the Affected component and Localization sections.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies that switch_dist_1_1's OSPF is missing the network 10.1.1.0/24 advertisement and recommends adding the OSPF network statement.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly describes an asymmetric failure: forward path works (uplink/OSPF learned) while the rest of the network has no route back to 10.1.1.0/24, causing return-path failure and dropped replies.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: The report notes the uplink network is advertised but fails to explicitly state that the switch's own pings source from its advertised uplink address (172.16.0.7), which is why replies reach the switch.
Correctly instructs adding the missing OSPF network statement (or redistributing the connected subnet) on switch_dist_1_1, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's observations and inferences directly support the conclusion.
